chose: Asking home to hear a take again (#3339) is one slice of state, `lib/hear-again`, that every screen showing takes composes, as they compose the play slice: Takes on home and Takes › Needs your attention today. It is offered on every take whose read carries `hearAgain` (paulgsc/server's `hear_again` act), heard ones included, as the owner widened it: a take marked heard can be mis-heard. The ask is enabled only while home says it can be asked now (`open`). Under it the take says while home is hearing it again, or until when home's snooze runs (`nextAt`; six hours by home's policy, C926). Home holds the snooze; the phone only shows what home last said, and a fresh read replaces what an answer laid over the take (a page of older takes does not). One ask is under way at a time, and on Needs your attention no act goes out while an ask is, nor an ask while an act is. An answer counts only for the ask made last. Home asked (201, or 200 for a resend) shows the take as being heard. Home's snooze (409 naming `nextAt`) shows when it can be asked again. A take home hasn't heard a first time (409 naming nothing) changes nothing and says so. A take home doesn't hold (404) can't be asked again: on Needs your attention it leaves the list, and the page says why. The ask is disabled by what home last said, not by this phone's clock, so a snooze that has run out lets the take be asked again on the next read (opening the page, a pull down).
options: one shared slice, offered on any take home says it re-hears (chosen)
a third act in Needs your attention's own act union (`ReconcileAct`): the first shape, but Takes would need a second copy of the same state
a re-hear button that asks home blind, with no snooze shown: nothing would say why a second tap does nothing
gray: Where the ask is offered, what disables it and what it says are on the screen; no check settles them.
undo: Drop the slice from the two machines and their screens, `hearAgain` from both reads and the ports, and `lib/hear-again` in soundbites and www.
